summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with acute-on-chronic low back pain radiating to the abdomen, two weeks after a sudden onset. Imaging revealed a new acute-to-subacute compression fracture at T11, with a stable chronic L5 fracture. She was managed conservatively with a back brace, morphine, oxycodone, and muscle relaxants, with spine surgery follow-up planned for possible vertebroplasty if needed. An MRCP showed multiple pancreatic cysts, likely side-branch IPMNs, with a recommendation for repeat MRI in six months. Her chronic conditions—GVHD, diabetes, osteoporosis, and history of DVT/PE—were maintained on current therapies, including enoxaparin, prednisone, sirolimus, and insulin. She remained stable, pain-controlled, and neurologically intact, and was discharged home with follow-up plans for spine and imaging.
